title: Aircraft Power Plants Test Cell Operator (GySgt to Cpl) NMOS (6122, 6123, 6124, 6216, 6222, 6223, 6227), DC AVN
raw_text:
8. MOS 6023, Aircraft Power Plants Test Cell Operator (GySgt to Cpl) NMOS
(6122, 6123, 6124, 6216, 6222, 6223, 6227), DC AVN

    a. Summary. Aircraft Power Plants Test Cell Operators, inspect, test,
and perform corrective maintenance to aircraft gas turbine engines and engine
systems. Perform test cell operations and minor repairs to test cells. This
MOS will be assigned only to qualified Aircraft Power Plants Mechanics, MOSs
6122, 6123, 6124, 6222, 6223, 6226, and 6227.

       b.   Prerequisites

        (1) Possess one of the following PMOSs 6122, 6123, 6124, 6216, 6222,
6223, 6226, and 6227.

        (2) Completed the Training and Readiness (T&R) 4000 SSSP in its
entirety for that respective PMOS.

    c. Requirements. Complete the respective type of engine test cell
training syllabus in Advanced Skills Management as per reference (ad)
COMNAVFORINST 4790.2 and (bn) NAVMC 4790.1.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (ad) COMNAVFORINST 4790.2 and (bn) NAVMC 4790.1.




                                           3-357                        Enclosure (1)
 3138                                                                 NAVMC 1200.1L



    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Aircraft Mechanics and Service Technicians 49-3011.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Helicopter Power Plants Mechanic, T-64, 6123.

            (2) Helicopter Power Plants Mechanic, T-400/T-700, 6124.

            (3) Fixed-Wing Power Plants Mechanic, F-402, 6222.

            (4) Fixed-Wing Power Plants Mechanic, J-52, 6223.

            (5) Fixed-Wing Power Plants Mechanic, T-56, 6226.

            (6) Fixed-Wing Power Plants Mechanic, F-404, 6227.

While there is similarity in the skills required to provide this support, the systems being supported are diverse.. The following examples are provided: direct support-repair and servicing at the organizational maintenance activity which is normally accomplished on aircraft, e.g., preflight and servicing of aircraft and their systems; indirect support-repair of components at the intermediate maintenance activity which is normally accomplished off aircraft, e.g., hydraulic actuators, servos, and accumulators, aircraft engines, and transmissions. Marines entering these fields receive MOS 6000, Basic Aircraft Maintenance Marine, and then progress through specific hard skill MOSs. After completion of formal training, Marines are qualified to maintain airframes and aircraft components. The opportunity to participate in a formal apprenticeship program leading to receipt of a Department of Labor Certification of Apprenticeship Completion maybe available in some MOSs within OccFlds 60/61/ 62. As the Marine progresses, repair and administrative requirements for multiple systems take on an equal importance until the Marine is placed in a management/supervisory position. Billets for both repair and administration are varied and extend from the squadron level to staff positions at the wing, force commander, and Headquarters U.S. Marine Corps level.

body:
The Aircraft Maintenance OccFlds includes direct and indirect support of the total airframes and power plant package of all aviation aircraft weapons systems. While there is similarity in the skills required to provide this support, the systems being supported are diverse.. The following examples are provided: direct support-repair and servicing at the organizational maintenance activity which is normally accomplished on aircraft, e.g., preflight and servicing of aircraft and their systems; indirect support-repair of components at the intermediate maintenance activity which is normally accomplished off aircraft, e.g., hydraulic actuators, servos, and accumulators, aircraft engines, and transmissions. Marines entering these fields receive MOS 6000, Basic Aircraft Maintenance Marine, and then progress through specific hard skill MOSs. After completion of formal training, Marines are qualified to maintain airframes and aircraft components. The opportunity to participate in a formal apprenticeship program leading to receipt of a Department of Labor Certification of Apprenticeship Completion maybe available in some MOSs within OccFlds 60/61/ 62. As the Marine progresses, repair and administrative requirements for multiple systems take on an equal importance until the Marine is placed in a management/supervisory position. Billets for both repair and administration are varied and extend from the squadron level to staff positions at the wing, force commander, and Headquarters U.S. Marine Corps level.

8. MOS 6023, Aircraft Power Plants Test Cell Operator (GySgt to Cpl) NMOS (6122, 6123, 6124, 6216, 6222, 6223, 6227), DC AVN a. Summary. Aircraft Power Plants Test Cell Operators, inspect, test, and perform corrective maintenance to aircraft gas turbine engines and engine systems. Perform test cell operations and minor repairs to test cells. This MOS will be assigned only to qualified Aircraft Power Plants Mechanics, MOSs 6122, 6123, 6124, 6222, 6223, 6226, and 6227. b. Prerequisites (1) Possess one of the following PMOSs 6122, 6123, 6124, 6216, 6222, 6223, 6226, and 6227. (2) Completed the Training and Readiness (T&R) 4000 SSSP in its entirety for that respective PMOS. c. Requirements. Complete the respective type of engine test cell training syllabus in Advanced Skills Management as per reference (ad) COMNAVFORINST 4790.2 and (bn) NAVMC 4790.1. d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (ad) COMNAVFORINST 4790.2 and (bn) NAVMC 4790.1.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
